paper_metadata.title: Poor nutritional status is associated with incomplete functional recovery in elderly patients with mild traumatic brain injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the baseline characteristics well. However, it is a single-center retrospective study and a significant number of eligible patients (146/403) were excluded due to missing blood tests, which may introduce selection bias as these patients might differ from those included.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (GNRI) is calculated using objective, standardized measurements (Albumin, weight, height) taken within a strict timeframe (24h).

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The GNRI was calculated as follows: GNRI = 1.489* albumin (g/L) + 41.7* [present body weight (kg)/ideal body weight (kg)].
items.reasoning: The mathematical formula and components are explicitly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: All blood markers were measured from the same peripheral blood sample, which was taken from patients within 24 h after injury.
items.reasoning: Measurements are based on objective laboratory tests and physical measurements rather than subjective recall.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (GOSE) was assessed via telephone, which introduces potential for subjective bias or recall bias. While GOSE is a validated tool, the lack of blinding of the assessors to the patients' nutritional status is not addressed.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The clinical outcome was divided into complete recovery (GOSE = 8) and incomplete recovery (GOSE ≤ 7) at 6 months after the injury.
items.reasoning: The outcome and timing are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: At 6 months after injury, we contacted patients by telephone to complete the questionnaire.
items.reasoning: GOSE is a validated tool, but telephone administration and lack of mention of assessor blinding increase risk of bias.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: A structured, validated questionnaire was applied to evaluate the GOSE (20). At 6 months after injury, we contacted patients by telephone
items.reasoning: The same telephone-based questionnaire method was used for all participants.
